sample_unit: ophthalmologist review responses on LLM-generated plain language summaries (plus 362 nonophthalmology respondents preferring PLS)

links.outcome: Errors in LLM plain language summaries identified on ophthalmologist review and their risk of harm
links.effect: PLS error rate on ophthalmologist review was 26% (126 of 489); 83.9% (104 of 126) of errors low risk for harm, none severe harm or death; errors persisted despite physician review.
links.quote: PLS error rate on ophthalmologist review was 26% (126 of 489).

links.outcome: Clinician understanding, satisfaction, clarity and readability of notes with vs without LLM plain language summary
links.effect: Diagnostic understanding +9.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.3-18.2); note detail satisfaction +21.5 points; explanation clarity +23.0 points; Flesch Reading Ease 51.8 vs 43.6.
links.quote: Nonophthalmology clinicians and professionals reported enhanced diagnostic understanding (percentage point increase, 9.0; 95% CI, 0.3-18.2; P = .01), increased note detail satisfaction (percentage point increase, 21.5; 95% CI, 11.4-31.5; P < .001), and improved explanation clarity (percentage point increase, 23.0; 95% CI, 12.0-33.1; P < .001) for notes containing a PLS.

screen.reason: This randomized quality improvement trial deployed LLM-generated plain language summaries into clinical ophthalmology notes and evaluated physician review time, error detection, and safety/accuracy in real practice.
